record.paper_title: Course 6 - Short-Range Spin Glasses: Selected Open Problems
record.original_question: For realistic finite-dimensional short-range spin glasses, what is the correct mathematical and physical order parameter for the putative low-temperature spin glass phase, and how should it capture the broken symmetry of that phase?

artifact.status_search_result: The identification of a correct order parameter (and corresponding pure-state / metastate structure) for finite-dimensional short-range spin glasses remains one of the central unresolved problems in the rigorous and physical theory of disordered systems. Recent works (e.g. Newman–Stein topical reviews, the 2025 preprint "Order parameter for non-mean-field spin glasses" by Castellana et al., and ongoing Griffiths-type and metastate analyses) continue to debate competing scenarios (RSB, droplet, chaotic pairs, TNT) without a consensus or proof, indicating the question is still open.

status_evidence.title: Newman and Stein: Spin Glasses (Open Problems in Mathematical Physics)
status_evidence.snippet: Lists the nature of the low-temperature phase and the proper order parameter of finite-dimensional spin glasses among basic unresolved problems.
status_evidence.claim: The proper order parameter for short-range spin glasses is listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Order parameter for non-mean-field spin glasses
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) preprint proposing an order parameter for non-mean-field spin glasses, indicating the problem is still actively investigated.
status_evidence.claim: The question is still being actively researched as of 2025.

status_evidence.title: Topical Review: Ordering and broken symmetry in short-ranged spin glasses (Newman–Stein)
